moved.sentence: **type-matches-query**: The index type **SHOULD** match how the column is queried, not default to B-tree reflexively:

judged.note: Matching index type to how the column is queried, not B-tree by reflex, is kept at SHOULD; the type table it introduced is carried whole by choose-the-type-by-access-pattern.

moved.sentence: The author **SHOULD** measure write impact before adding one, and **SHOULD** prefer an expression index on a single extracted scalar key when that is all queries need.

judged.note: Both SHOULDs are kept: measure GIN write impact before adding one, and prefer an expression index on a single extracted scalar key when that is all queries need.

moved.sentence: Examples below assume PostgreSQL 16/17; pin behavior to your server's version.

judged.note: The PostgreSQL 16/17 assumption is kept and pinning behavior to the server's version is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **measured-need**: Specialized strategies — BRIN on huge append-only tables, table partitioning, custom operator classes — are adopt-only-when-a-concrete-measured-need-justifies-it, not defaults (YAGNI; make-it-work, make-it-right, make-it-fast).

judged.note: Adopting BRIN, partitioning and custom operator classes only on a concrete measured need, not as defaults, is kept at SHOULD with all three examples and the YAGNI reasons.
